Map the gateway's files, then deploy them with GitHub Actions

READ FIRST

How this assignment works

  • Share your screen in your breakout room: this is a "look over your shoulder" class, so we drop in where it's useful.
  • scripts/setup.sh is safe to re-run. It waits until every gateway is RUNNING; a cold start takes a few minutes.
  • Trial mode is fine. Each gateway runs a 2-hour trial. Reset it when necessary (Platform → Licensing → Reset Trial).
  • exercises/lab.md is the source of truth. These slides summarise it; when they differ, follow lab.md.
Ask earlyStuck for more than a couple of minutes? Say so in the room. docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md covers the common stack, runner and deploy failures, including a port that is already taken.

SETUP

Open this lab, require approval for outside PRs, start the stack

  1. Get the latest course version (from any folder of your clone): it replaces your main, here and on your fork, so no merge conflicts.
  2. Go to this lab's folder in your clone and open it in VS Code.
  3. Require approval for outside PRs: Settings → Actions → General → Approval for running fork pull request workflows from contributors → Require approval for all external contributors → Save. Your fork is public and this lab's runner holds the Docker socket.
  4. Start the stack: three gateways, TimescaleDB and the runner. setup.sh warns if .env has no runner URL or PAT yet.
# 1: latest course version on main, here and on your fork
#    (replaces your main: no merge conflicts)
git fetch https://github.com/Mustry-Academy/cicd-for-ignition.git main \
  && git checkout -f -B main FETCH_HEAD && git push -f origin main

# 2: this lab's folder
cd ~/mustry-academy/cicd-for-ignition
cd labs/04-ignition-file-based-deploy
code .

# 3: the same setting from the CLI
R=<you>/cicd-for-ignition
echo '{"approval_policy":"all_external_contributors"}' \
  | gh api -X PUT --input - \
    repos/$R/actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval

# 4: start the stack
scripts/setup.sh
Push rejected by a rule violation?Lab 03's protect-main ruleset is still on your fork: Settings › Rules › Rulesets › protect-main › Delete ruleset, then run step 1 again.

PART 1 · WE DO

Tour data/ and catch a UI change on disk

  1. Tour. ls -la the gateway's data/ from inside the container and put every top-level entry in a bucket: project, gateway or operational.
  2. Find the file. Touch /tmp/marker, change the Welcome Screen Notes in Platform → Gateway Settings, then find -newer the file it wrote. Note the scope in its path.
  3. Again with a DB connection. Re-touch the marker, create a Postgres connection Scratch (Connect URL jdbc:postgresql://timescaledb:5432/ignition_local_development, user ignition, Password Embedded: ignition), find -newer, then git status. Which deployment-mode collection did it land in, and why does that matter for test vs production?
# 1: the tour
docker exec -it lab04-ignition-local bash -lc \
  "ls -la /usr/local/bin/ignition/data"

# 2-3: set a marker, click in the UI, find what changed
docker exec lab04-ignition-local touch /tmp/marker
#    ... make the change in the gateway UI ...
docker exec lab04-ignition-local find \
  /usr/local/bin/ignition/data/config -newer /tmp/marker -type f
git status                 # the same files, in your repo
PART 1 · WE DO

Read connections, devices, tags and deployment modes as files

  1. Everything is a file. Open the shipped TimescaleDB connection, the Simulator device and the example-tags tag definitions.
  2. Deployment modes: diff the local-development vs production connection. Exactly one line differs.
# 4: under services/config/resources/core/
ignition/database-connection/TimescaleDB/config.json
com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device/Simulator/config.json
ignition/tag-definition/example-tags/tags.json

# 5: deployment modes, one per-mode override
diff services/config/resources/local-development/ignition/database-connection/TimescaleDB/config.json \
     services/config/resources/production/ignition/database-connection/TimescaleDB/config.json

PART 2 · WE DO

Deploy a view to test by hand, then read .deployignore

  1. Edit a view that already exists: in example-project's overview view.json, change the label text "Run Control" to "Run Control v2". Local bind-mounts ./projects/, so this is editing local's disk.
  2. Run scripts/scan.sh, open localhost:8088/data/perspective/client/example-project: the top-left card reads RUN CONTROL V2.
  3. Ship to test by hand: docker cp the project, scan. Test starts empty, so nothing to wipe. Verify at localhost:8089/…/example-project.
  4. Read .deployignore: for each pattern, say why the gateway shouldn't have that file.
# 1: projects/example-project/com.inductiveautomation
#      .perspective/views/pages/overview/view.json
#    "text": "Run Control" → "Run Control v2"

# 2 (local): just scan, then verify at :8088
scripts/scan.sh

# 3 (test): copy the project over, then scan the test gateway
docker cp ./projects/. \
  lab04-ignition-test:/usr/local/bin/ignition/data/projects/
scripts/scan.sh test
ls gateways/test/projects   # on the host

# 4: what never lands on a gateway
cat .deployignore
Red null values on test are expectedYou copied only the project: test has no tags or connections yet. The first real deploy ships the config too.
PARTS 2.1 · 2.2

Runner online, then GitHub environments and secrets

  1. Verify the runner (part of the compose stack). In your fork, Settings → Actions → Runners shows it online with labels self-hosted, lab04.
  2. Not there? RUNNER_REPO_URL points at your fork · RUNNER_GITHUB_PAT is a real fine-grained PAT with the rights on the right (a bad one shows a 401 or 403 in the logs) · then docker compose up -d --force-recreate github-runner.
  3. On GitHub, in your fork: environment lab04-gateway-test (Settings → Environments → New environment) with secret IGNITION_API_KEY = IGNITION_API_KEY_TEST from .env (:8089).
  4. Repeat: lab04-gateway-production with IGNITION_API_KEY_PRODUCTION (:8090). Leave IGNITION_URL / IGNITION_CONTAINER as is.
# part 2.1: is the runner alive?
docker compose ps github-runner
docker compose logs --tail 50 github-runner
# look for "Listening for Jobs"
Runner PAT
Fine-grained: Settings › Developer settings › Fine-grained tokens
Repository access
Only select repositories › <you>/cicd-for-ignition
Permission
Administration: Read and write (Metadata: Read-only comes with it)
Why
The runner uses it to fetch its own registration token
PART 2.3

Create sample-project and commit it on a feature branch

  1. Create a project sample-project on the local gateway (Designer → New Project, or Platform → Projects). The bind mount drops it into your working tree: that folder is your deployable.
  2. Create one simple view in the Designer (e.g. a label with your name). Tick Page URL (/) in the New View dialog so a browser can open it. Save. No Designer? Write the view on disk with the minimal 8.3 content from docs/ignition-file-structure.md, then scripts/scan.sh.
  3. Branch feature/add-sample-project off main, git add projects/ and commit (this also picks up the Run Control v2 edit), then push.
# 1-2: create project + view in Ignition, then look at the repo
git status              # untracked: projects/sample-project/

# 3: the feature branch
git switch main
git switch -c feature/add-sample-project
git add projects/
git commit -m "Add sample-project"
git push -u origin feature/add-sample-project
PART 2.3

Open the PR, merge into main, and verify the test gateway

  1. Open a PR into main, base repository <you>/cicd-for-ignition (your fork). Watch lab04-ci.yml on ubuntu-latest: yamllint, actionlint, shellcheck, ign-lint, docker compose config, JSON validity, .deployignore syntax, the security-properties identity check.
  2. Merge. lab04-deploy.yml fires (its paths: filter skips docs-only pushes). Watch Ship and Trigger gateway scan. The first deploy to a fresh gateway restarts it once; later ones scan hot.
  3. Verify at localhost:8089. Platform → Projects lists sample-project; its view opens at …/data/perspective/client/sample-project; RUN CONTROL V2 now shows live values.
# then on GitHub: PR into main → CI green → merge

# 6: after the deploy, see what CI shipped
ls gateways/test/projects
# example-project  packaging-site  sample-project:
# one deploy ships the whole projects/ tree
Nothing deployed?Two classic causes: the change didn't touch a deploy path (the paths: filter skipped it), or Actions isn't enabled on your fork.
PART 2.4

Release to production: tag the commit on main

  1. The tag is what ships production. The merge already shipped test; the change is on main, so you only tag it.
  2. Tag lab04-v0.1.0 and push the tag: lab04-release.yml runs the same five steps against the production container. Tag already taken? Use the next free number; git tag -l shows what's taken.
  3. Verify at localhost:8090 (or Designer). Host check: ls gateways/production/projects.
# on main, the change is already there from the test deploy
git switch main && git pull

git tag lab04-v0.1.0
git push origin lab04-v0.1.0        # ← lab04-release.yml fires
PART 2.5

Break a deploy on purpose, then read the failure

  1. Wrong API key. Garbage in lab04-gateway-test's secret, re-run. Ship succeeds (docker cp doesn't care about keys), the scan gets a 401 and fails fast. Files are on disk, but the gateway keeps running the old state. Your recovery story?
  2. Stopped container. docker compose stop ignition-test, then deploy. The prerequisites check fails fast ("container is in state 'exited', expected 'running'") before any file moved.
  3. Fix it and re-run (manual workflow_dispatch works too). The steps are idempotent: the deploy converges.
# failure B: stop the target, watch verify fail fast
docker compose stop ignition-test
# … re-run lab04-deploy.yml from the Actions tab …
docker compose up -d ignition-test  # recovery

Write it down for the debrief

  1. Symptomwhat the run shows
  2. Gateway stateon disk vs running
  3. Recoveryhow you fix it
  4. Earlier catch?which workflow step should have caught it

Definition of done for Part 1 and Part 2

PART 1Without peeking, you can

  • List the top-level data/ entries and give each its bucket.
  • Find the file a UI change wrote, with the /tmp/marker + find -newer trick.
  • State the 8.3 path shape for a view (projects/<x>/com.inductiveautomation.perspective/views/… + resource.json) and a config resource (config/resources/<scope>/<module>/<type>/<name>/config.json).
  • Point at the file for a DB connection, a device connection and a tag definition, and say why "it's all in git" follows.
  • Explain deployment modes in one sentence and name what differs between the local-development and production TimescaleDB connection.
  • Explain why db/ and .resources/ must not be committed.

PART 2Your fork and gateways show

  • The bundled runner online in your fork (self-hosted, lab04).
  • Both environments (lab04-gateway-test, lab04-gateway-production), each with an IGNITION_API_KEY secret.
  • A push to main ran lab04-deploy.yml: your project is on test (:8089).
  • A lab04-v* tag on main ran lab04-release.yml: it is on production (:8090).
  • You broke one deploy on purpose and can describe failure and recovery.
  • You can name the routing (push to main → test, tag on main → production) and the five steps between "merge" and "gateway reloaded".

OPTIONAL · 2

Stretch: why copy and scan can't deploy a module

Not shipped

Module enablement lives in services/modules.json, a sibling of services/config/. Both workflows copy ./services/config/., so it is not shipped. Local mounts services/modules.json; test and production boot from their own copy in gateways/<gw>/, seeded once by setup.sh. Open lab04-deploy.yml and confirm the docker cp targets.

Not applied by a scan

Even with a new modules.json on the gateway, enabling or disabling a module needs a restart (docker compose restart ignition-test), unlike views and config.

The question to chew onList everything else a scan could never apply (memory, Java args, module binaries…). What does that tell you about where the image-based deploy of Lab 05 earns its keep?

You built a pipeline that ships Ignition

  • Runner online, both environments hold an API key, a push to main deployed test, a lab04-v* tag deployed production, and one deploy broke and recovered.
  • The five steps between "merge" and "gateway reloaded", and the routing: push to main → test, tag on main → production, local outside the flow.
  • For the debrief: your Part 2.5 failure story, your rollback answer (revert on main vs re-deploy a tag), and where a runner would sit at your customer's site.
